comment: Non-reactive silicate mineral ("non-degradable natural component of the environment"); documented chronic hazard is inhalation-driven (pneumoconiosis/"Kaolinosis"), not environmental accumulation; no KFOC/KOC data.

Chemically the same substance as kaolin (identical DT50 notes, word for word), only thermally processed. PPDB labels it Substance origin = Synthetic (a production classification, not a chemistry one) - included here for consistency with kaolin rather than by reading that field. No DT50/KFOC/KOC data at all. Has a real chronic aquatic invertebrate NOEC in the PPDB - the reason k_water is not overridden for this list ("HPLI methodology.md", section "Where the persistence coefficient is applied") - whether that specific exposure pathway is itself persistence-related has not been checked.
Crystalline silica, "stable in soil"; documented chronic hazard is inhalation-driven (silicosis), not accumulation; no KFOC/KOC data.

Same chemical family as quartz sand (SiO2), "stable in soil"; explicit US EPA note on lung cancer from inhaled crystalline silica particles - same inhalation mechanism, not accumulation; no KFOC/KOC data.

Diatomaceous earth (SiO2)n, natural origin, "stable in soil"; documented chronic hazard is inhalation-driven (pneumoconiosis/bronchitis/emphysema), same mechanism as the other silicates above; no KFOC/KOC data.

Natural mineral, "unlikely to cause environmental fate issues"; cleanest of the six - no carcinogenicity/genotoxicity/reprotoxicity/neurotoxicity flags at all, only a minor "possible" respiratory irritation note; no KFOC/KOC data. Has a real chronic aquatic fish NOEC in the PPDB (its invertebrate NOEC is itself missing) - the reason k_water is not overridden for this list ("HPLI methodology.md", section "Where the persistence coefficient is applied"); whether that specific exposure pathway is itself persistence-related has not been checked.

Matches the same "stable in soil" wording as the included group, but is a heavy-metal (barium) compound with documented "chronic barium poisoning" - a real accumulation-type mechanism, not inert. Has a real soil DT50 already; only KFOC/KOC are missing, and the standard precautionary default is kept for it.
